race_context: The district: Medora Community School Corporation in Medora, Jackson County, runs two schools, Medora STEM Academy and Medora Jr./Sr. High, in one building at 82 South George Street {med_home}{wiki_mjshs}. It is one of Indiana's smallest districts: state data show 184 students in 2026 and 185 in 2025 {idoe_enroll}. Roger Bane is superintendent {med_agenda_2026_10_19}{med_min_2024_05_13}.

Board: five trustees. Joe Campbell is president, Darrell Persinger vice president and Ada Reynolds secretary; Faythe Gill and Tony Hall are the other members {med_min_2026_01_12}. State results list two races: 'Seats 1, 2, & 3' (three seats, last elected in 2024: Campbell, Gill and Anthony J. Hall) and 'Seats 4 & 5' (two seats, last elected in 2022) {enr_2024}{enr_2022}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: TWO seats, Seats 4 and 5. The state list shows 'vote for 1', but state results list this race as electing two members in both 2018 and 2022 {in_list}{enr_2018}{enr_2022}. In 2022 Darrell Persinger (268 votes) and Larry Osborn (176) were elected unopposed {enr_2022}. Osborn resigned effective December 31, 2023, and on January 15, 2024 the board appointed Ada Reynolds to replace him for a term running to December 31, 2026 {med_min_2024_01_15}. Both incumbents, Persinger and Reynolds, are running, and they are the only two candidates for the two seats {in_list}. Voters should check their sample ballot for how many candidates to choose.
Party labels: Persinger is listed as a Republican and Reynolds as Nonpartisan {in_list}. Persinger ran without a party label in 2018 and 2022, when none were allowed {enr_2018}{enr_2022}.

Budget: the board has repeatedly moved money from the Education Fund to the Operations Fund, including $100,000 transfers approved in October 2025, December 2025 and September 2026 {med_min_2025_10_13}{med_min_2025_12_08}{med_min_2026_09_14}. On September 14, 2026 it voted 5-0 to reduce 2026 appropriations in the Operations, Rainy Day and Education funds and held the public hearing on the 2027 budget, bus replacement plan and capital projects plan {med_min_2026_09_14}. Adoption of the 2027 budget and the purchase of a 15-passenger activity bus are on the October 19, 2026 agenda {med_agenda_2026_10_19}. This guide found no public statement from the board on how the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects Medora's budget. Medora is not listed among districts with a school tax referendum on the November 2026 ballot {dlgf_ref}.

Facilities and debt: in 2024 the board approved a $1,770,500 HVAC bid from Harrell-Fish Inc. and an amended lease with the Medora 1999 School Building Corporation to finance HVAC and roofing improvements to the school building {med_min_2024_05_13}. In 2026 the superintendent held preliminary determination hearings on a new bond project on March 9 and April 13. On April 13 the board voted 4-0 for the preliminary determination/bond resolution and an additional appropriation to spend the bond proceeds; no members of the public commented {med_min_2026_03_09}{med_min_2026_04_13}. The minutes do not describe the project or its amount.

Staffing and academics: on November 10, 2025 the board ratified a teachers' contract with the Medora Classroom Teachers Association (MCTA) covering July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2027 {med_min_2025_10_13}{med_min_2025_11_10}. In April 2025 the principal reported that Medora Jr./Sr. High was chosen for a Notre Dame AP program cohort that lets students earn college credit {med_min_2025_04_14}. The board renewed a career and technical education agreement with North Lawrence schools in 2025 and 2026 {med_min_2025_04_14}{med_min_2026_07_13}.
Forums: this guide found no candidate forum, questionnaire or news profile for this race.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and board secretary, appointed in January 2024 to fill a vacancy, and listed as Nonpartisan {med_min_2024_01_15}{med_min_2026_01_12}{in_list}.
background: Appointed to the board on January 15, 2024 to replace Larry Osborn, who resigned effective December 31, 2023 {med_min_2024_01_15}. Has been board secretary since January 2025 and was reappointed secretary in January 2026 {med_min_2025_01_13}{med_min_2026_01_12}.

path_to_ballot: Filed on May 27, 2026, according to a list compiled from state filings, and is listed as Nonpartisan {incitizen_list}{in_list}. This is her first time on the ballot for this board; she joined it by appointment {med_min_2024_01_15}{enr_2022}.
on_incumbent: Is a current board member. This guide found no public statements from her about the board's record; the posted minutes record no remarks under 'items by School Board members' at the meetings reviewed {med_min_2026_09_14}.

She made the motions to approve the May 2024 HVAC bid, to ratify the 2025-2027 teachers' contract in November 2025, to approve the April 2026 bond resolution and to reduce 2026 appropriations in September 2026. All passed with no votes against {med_min_2024_05_13}{med_min_2025_11_10}{med_min_2026_04_13}{med_min_2026_09_14}.
She is recorded as present at 18 of the 20 board meetings from January 2025 through September 2026 whose posted minutes this guide could read {med_min_2025_06_09}{med_min_2025_10_13}.
